#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Homebrew and the Brewfile: install what the deployed Brewfile declares and is missing, never remove anything.
# What brew-file would remove is only reported: formulae and taps from `brew file clean --dry-run`, casks by comparison.
# Brewfile hash: {{ include "dot_config/brewfile/Brewfile" | sha256sum }}
{{ template "script-lib.sh" "brew" }}

load_brew {{ .brew.prefix | squote }}
brewfile=${HOMEBREW_BREWFILE:-$HOME/.config/brewfile/Brewfile}

# The Brewfile is a deployed target: a missing one means the apply did not write it, and brew-file would
# create a new one from the installed packages instead of installing anything.
if [ ! -f "$brewfile" ]; then
  warn "$brewfile is missing"
  exit 1
fi

if ! have brew || ! brew file version > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "Homebrew or brew-file is missing: running the brew-file installer"
  # Homebrew's installer calls sudo; NONINTERACTIVE=1 makes it use cached credentials and never ask, so cache them here.
  if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    as_root "cache sudo credentials for the Homebrew installer" -v
  fi
  run env NONINTERACTIVE=1 bash -c 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcmdnk/homebrew-file/install/install.sh | bash'
  load_brew {{ .brew.prefix | squote }}
fi

if ! have brew; then
  if dry_run; then
    log "brew is not installed: the rest of this script needs it, stopping after the dry run"
    exit 0
  fi
  warn "brew is still missing after the installer"
  exit 1
fi

log "brew file install from $brewfile"
run brew file install

# Completions of the formulae and taps: the link is a persistent state that Homebrew keeps up on install, upgrade
# and update. The shell startup used to run `brew completions link` at every start (about 0.7 s); it runs here, once.
case "$(brew completions state 2> /dev/null || true)" in
  'Completions are linked.'*) ;;
  *)
    log "brew completions are not linked: linking them"
    run brew completions link
    ;;
esac

# Drift report, read only: nothing below installs, uninstalls or untaps.
# brew-file ignores casks on Linux, so the casks are compared here; formulae and taps come from its own dry run.
if clean_out=$(brew file clean --dry-run 2>&1); then
  report_undeclared "brew formulae" "$(printf '%s\n' "$clean_out" | sed -n 's/^\$ brew uninstall --ignore-dependencies //p' | tr ' ' '\n')" ""
  report_undeclared "brew taps" "$(printf '%s\n' "$clean_out" | sed -n 's/^\$ brew untap //p' | tr ' ' '\n')" ""
else
  warn "brew file clean --dry-run failed: no report for formulae and taps"
fi

report_undeclared "brew casks" "$(brew list --cask 2> /dev/null || true)" "$declared_casks"

if have gh && ! gh auth status > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  warn "gh is not logged in: run 'gh auth login' in a terminal"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the mise tools that the deployed global config declares and that are missing, then refresh the shims.
# Nothing is pruned: no tool version is removed, only the generated shims are brought in line with what is installed.
# mise config hash: {{ include "dot_config/mise/config.toml" | sha256sum }}
# tools: {{ template "tools-present" (dict "root" . "tools" (list "mise")) }}
{{ template "script-lib.sh" "mise" }}

load_brew {{ .brew.prefix | squote }}
{{ template "tools-use" . }}

need mise || exit 0

log "mise install"
run mise install --yes

# Shim cleanup. A shim is a generated link in the mise shims directory, one per executable of an installed tool.
# After a tool is uninstalled or its directory is deleted, its shim can stay behind: the shim then counts as a present tool
# for the tools-present line of the other scripts, and fails with "No version is set" when run.
# `mise reshim` adds the missing shims and removes the mise-owned ones that no installed tool provides any more;
# it leaves every other file of the directory alone, and does nothing on an up-to-date machine.
log "mise reshim"
run mise reshim

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the pipx venvs of the deployed spec file that are missing, through a copy of the file that holds only them,
# and report the installed venvs that the file does not declare. Nothing is removed or upgraded.
# The spec file holds no path and no interpreter; refresh it with:
#   pipx list --json | jq --indent 4 '(.. | objects | select(has("app_paths"))) |= (.app_paths = [] | .app_paths_of_dependencies = {} | .man_paths = [] | .man_paths_of_dependencies = {} | .completion_paths = [] | .completion_paths_of_dependencies = {}) | .venvs[].metadata.source_interpreter = null'
# packages.json hash: {{ include "dot_config/pipx/packages.json" | sha256sum }}
# tools: {{ template "tools-present" (dict "root" . "tools" (list "pipx" "jq")) }}
{{ template "script-lib.sh" "pipx" }}

load_brew {{ .brew.prefix | squote }}
{{ template "tools-use" . }}

need pipx jq || exit 0

spec=$HOME/.config/pipx/packages.json
if [ ! -f "$spec" ]; then
  warn "$spec is missing"
  exit 1
fi

declared=$(jq -r '.venvs | keys[]' "$spec")
installed=$(pipx list --short | awk '{ print $1 }')
missing=$(LC_ALL=C comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$installed" | LC_ALL=C sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$declared" | LC_ALL=C sort -u))

if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
  log "missing venvs: $(printf '%s' "$missing" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  if dry_run; then
    log "would run: pipx install-all on a copy of the spec file that holds only these venvs"
  else
    # Inside $HOME on purpose: nothing is written outside it.
    mkdir -p "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}"
    work=$(mktemp -d "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/pipx-spec.XXXXXX")
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    names=$(printf '%s\n' "$missing" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
    jq --argjson names "$names" '.venvs |= with_entries(select(.key as $k | $names | index($k) != null))' "$spec" > "$work/packages.json"
    run pipx install-all "$work/packages.json"
  fi
else
  log "all declared venvs are installed"
fi

report_undeclared "pipx venvs" "$installed" "$declared"
{{ end -}}

=== .chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20-vscodium-extensions.sh.tmpl
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" -}}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the VSCodium extensions of vscodium.extensions that are missing, then the local .vsix files whose extension is not
# installed. Never removes or upgrades anything. A failed install is a warning, not a failure: one extension that Open VSX does
# not offer must not stop the apply, and chezmoi would not retry the script until the list changes anyway.
# The list is in .chezmoidata/vscodium.yaml; its hash makes chezmoi re-run this script whenever the list changes.
# The .vsix directory is outside the repository, so adding a file there does not re-run the script.
# extensions hash: {{ .vscodium.extensions | toJson | sha256sum }}
# tools: {{ template "tools-present" (dict "root" . "tools" (list "codium")) }}
{{ template "script-lib.sh" "vscodium-extensions" }}

load_brew {{ .brew.prefix | squote }}
{{ template "tools-use" . }}

extensions=({{ range .vscodium.extensions }}{{ . | squote }} {{ end }})
vsix_dir=$HOME/.local/share/vsix

need codium || exit 0

# Without the list every extension would look missing: stop rather than install blindly.
if ! listing=$(codium --list-extensions 2> /dev/null); then
  warn "codium --list-extensions failed: nothing is installed"
  exit 1
fi
# Extension ids are case-insensitive: compare in lower case.
installed=$(printf '%s\n' "$listing" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

for ext in "${extensions[@]}"; do
  if grep -qxF "${ext,,}" <<< "$installed"; then
    continue
  fi
  log "installing $ext"
  if run codium --install-extension "$ext"; then
    installed+=$'\n'"${ext,,}"
  else
    warn "failed: $ext"
  fi
done

# vsix_id <file>: the extension id (publisher.name) of a .vsix, from the package.json inside it;
# without unzip or jq, or when the file is not a readable archive, the file name without its version suffix.
vsix_id() {
  local file=$1 id=''
  if have unzip && have jq; then
    id=$(unzip -p "$file" extension/package.json 2> /dev/null | jq -r 'select(.publisher and .name) | .publisher + "." + .name' 2> /dev/null || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$id" ]; then
    id=$(basename "$file" .vsix | sed -E 's/-[0-9]+(\.[0-9A-Za-z+_@-]*)*$//')
  fi
  printf '%s' "${id,,}"
}

# Extensions that are not on Open VSX: .vsix files kept outside this repository.
# A .vsix whose extension is already installed is skipped, whatever its version: upgrading it is a manual action.
shopt -s nullglob
for vsix in "$vsix_dir"/*.vsix; do
  id=$(vsix_id "$vsix")
  if [ -z "$id" ]; then
    warn "$(basename "$vsix"): cannot tell which extension it holds, skipped"
    continue
  fi
  if grep -qxF "$id" <<< "$installed"; then
    log "$(basename "$vsix"): $id is installed, skipped"
    continue
  fi
  log "installing $id from $vsix"
  if run codium --install-extension "$vsix"; then
    installed+=$'\n'"$id"
  else
    warn "failed: $vsix"
  fi
done
{{- end }}

=== .chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_21-vim-plugins.sh.tmpl
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" -}}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Vundle plugins that the deployed vimrc declares (Vundle itself is a chezmoi external, already in place).
# Build the YouCompleteMe core library only when vim.ycm_build is true and the library is missing.
# vimrc hash: {{ include "dot_config/vim/vimrc" | sha256sum }}
# tools: {{ template "tools-present" (dict "root" . "tools" (list "vim")) }}
# Vim is a secondary editor since Neovim became the main one; this script only keeps its Vundle plugins in place.
{{ template "script-lib.sh" "vim-plugins" }}

load_brew {{ .brew.prefix | squote }}
{{ template "tools-use" . }}

ycm_build={{ .vim.ycm_build }}
vimrc=$HOME/.vimrc
bundle=$HOME/.vim/bundle

need vim || exit 0

if [ ! -f "$vimrc" ] || [ ! -d "$bundle/Vundle.vim" ]; then
  warn "$vimrc or $bundle/Vundle.vim is missing: the vimrc and the Vundle external come with the apply"
  exit 1
fi

log "vim PluginInstall"
# Ex mode, silent, no viminfo, no swap file: plugins that are already present are left alone.
# -N is required: Ex mode starts vi-compatible, which drops line continuations, and Vundle's own autoload file then fails (E10).
if ! run vim -N -Es -n -u "$vimrc" -i NONE +PluginInstall +qall; then
  warn "vim exited with an error: the plugins may be incomplete"
fi

if [ "$ycm_build" = true ]; then
  ycm=$bundle/YouCompleteMe
  if [ ! -f "$ycm/install.py" ]; then
    warn "vim.ycm_build is true but $ycm is not installed"
  elif compgen -G "$ycm/third_party/ycmd/ycm_core*.so" > /dev/null; then
    log "YouCompleteMe core library already built"
  elif have python3; then
    log "building the YouCompleteMe core library"
    run python3 "$ycm/install.py" --all
  else
    warn "python3 not found: cannot build YouCompleteMe"
  fi
fi
{{ end -}}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rebuild the bat cache (the custom themes and syntaxes of ~/.config/bat) when its inputs change.
# It writes only the cache directory of bat, inside $HOME, and rebuilding gives the same cache.
# bat reads the themes and syntaxes folders next to its config file, not the config file itself: the themes come from the
# externals, so the externals declaration is the real input; the config is hashed as well, because a theme choice is made there.
# Not covered: the upstream theme files, which the weekly refresh of the externals may change without re-running this script.
# bat config hash: {{ include "dot_config/bat/config" | sha256sum }}
# bat externals hash: {{ include ".chezmoiexternals/bat.toml.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
# tools: {{ template "tools-present" (dict "root" . "tools" (list "bat")) }}
{{ template "script-lib.sh" "bat-cache" }}

load_brew {{ .brew.prefix | squote }}
{{ template "tools-use" . }}

need bat || exit 0

log "bat cache --build"
run bat cache --build
{{ end -}}

=== .chezmoitemplates/tools-present
{{- /*
  "tool=present tool=absent ...": whether each tool of .tools is an executable in one of the directories of tools-dirs,
  for the hash comment of a script that skips when a tool is missing.
  The lookup never reads the PATH of the process that renders (findExecutable gets the list), so an interactive shell,
  cron and `env -i` render the same text, and the script runs again exactly when a tool appears or disappears there.
  Included with: template "tools-present" (dict "root" . "tools" (list "jq" "pipx"))
*/ -}}
{{- $home := .root.chezmoi.homeDir -}}
{{- $dirs := list -}}
{{- range (includeTemplate "tools-dirs" .root | fromJson) -}}
{{-   if hasPrefix "~/" . -}}
{{-     $dirs = append $dirs (joinPath $home (trimPrefix "~/" .)) -}}
{{-   else -}}
{{-     $dirs = append $dirs . -}}
{{-   end -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- range $i, $tool := .tools -}}
{{- if $i }} {{ end -}}
{{ $tool }}={{ if findExecutable $tool $dirs }}present{{ else }}absent{{ end }}
{{- end -}}

=== .chezmoitemplates/tools-use
{{- /*
  The call that gives a script the same directories as its tools-present line: use_tool_dirs '<dir>' '<dir>' ...
  A "~/x" entry is passed with its literal tilde on purpose: use_tool_dirs expands it to $HOME/x when it runs.
  Included with: template "tools-use" .   (the root context)
*/ -}}
# shellcheck disable=SC2088
use_tool_dirs{{ range (includeTemplate "tools-dirs" . | fromJson) }} {{ . | squote }}{{ end }}
